facts.text: Wolfeboro earned its name in 1759 when colonial Governor Benning Wentworth honored General James Wolfe, the victor at the Plains of Abraham.
The Clark Museum, run by the Wolfeboro Historical Society, showcases the town’s rich history through curated exhibits and engaging displays.
Wolfeboro sits at the head of Wolfeboro Bay on Lake Winnipesaukee, where the Smith River flows into the lake.
Known as “The Oldest Summer Resort in America,” Wolfeboro attracted Boston families in the 19th century as a seasonal retreat.
Celebrities like Prince Rainier, Grace of Monaco, Kurt Vonnegut, Drew Barrymore, and Jimmy Fallon have spent vacations in Wolfeboro.
In 2025 the Wolfeboro Historical Society received a proclamation from Governor Kelly Ayotte, celebrating 100 years of museum excellence.
